SNP-based Heritability

This section shows the output from LD-score regression, including an estimate of SNP-based heritability on the observed scale, and the LD-score regression intercept. The intercept can be used to determine whether there is genome-wide inflation that is not explained by high polygenicity.

SNP associations

This section list independent SNP associations achieving either genome-wide or suggestive significance. Independence is determined using LD-based clumping and/or conditional-joint (COJO analysis. Note, LD is estimated using a reference sample and may not accurately reflect the LD structure in the GWAS sample. COJO analysis is particularly sensitive to LD mispecification.

Clumped: GW-significant loci

GWAS contain 17 independent (r2 < 0.1, 500kb) genome-wide significant variants (p < 5e-8).

Full results file: results/ALS2021/clump/ALS2021.GW.clump.clean.csv

Note. CHR = Chromsome; BP = Basepair position; SNP = Variant ID; A1 = Allele 1 (effect allele); A2 = Allele 2 (reference allele); BETA = Effect size; SE = Standard error; P = p-value; FREQ = Frequency of allele 1 reported in GWAS; REF.FREQ = Frequency of allele 1 reported in ancestry matched reference population; N = Sample size; NearestGene = Nearest genes to lead variant with distance in parentheses

Clumped: Suggestive loci

Clumping finds 83 independent (r2 < 0.1, 500kb) suggestive significant variants (p < 1e-5).

Full results file: results/ALS2021/clump/ALS2021.GW.clump.clean.csv

Note. CHR = Chromsome; BP = Basepair position; SNP = Variant ID; A1 = Allele 1 (effect allele); A2 = Allele 2 (reference allele); BETA = Effect size; SE = Standard error; P = p-value; FREQ = Frequency of allele 1 reported in GWAS; REF.FREQ = Frequency of allele 1 reported in ancestry matched reference population; N = Sample size; NearestGene = Nearest genes to lead variant with distance in parentheses

SNP Finemapping

This section summarises the results SNP-based statistical finemapping, using the software SuSiE. Note, LD is estimated using a reference sample and may not accurately reflect the LD structure in the GWAS sample. Finemapping analysis is particularly sensitive to LD mispecification.

Finemapping: All loci

Full results file: results/ALS2021/finemap/ALS2021.GW.finemap.csv

Note. CHR = Chromsome; BP = Basepair position; SNP = Variant ID; cs = Credible set number; NSNP = Number of SNPs in 95% credible set; TopPIP = Highest posterior inclusion probability of variants within 95% credible set; Gene = Genes boundaries (+/- 10kb) all variants within 95% credible set.

Molecular associations

This section summarises analyses that infer molecular changes associated with the GWAS phenotype, either altered gene expression or protein levels. We integrate a range of datasets indicating the effect of genetic variants on expression and protein levels in different tissues. Depending on the availability of data, we run the analysis using FUSION or SMR

Summary of Molecular Associations

This section summarises gene-level association results from MAGMA, TWAS, PWAS, and SMR. This simply shows the whether genes showed a statistically significant association with the GWAS phenotype, and for TWAS/PWAS/SMR whether the association for gene expression/protein levels and the GWAS phenotype colocalised (same causal variant) and are consistent with a causal model.

Comparison of Methods

Drug repurposing

This section shows results drug repurposing analyses. Several analysis approaches are available. The inferred differential expression results from TWAS can be compared to the drug-induced expression profiles from the Connectivity Map, AKA LINCS, to identify drugs that induce expression profiles opposite expression profiles associated with the GWAS phenotype. Two methods are used to compare TWAS and CMAP profiles, including the average rank based method from So et al. and TWAS-GSEA from Pain et al. An alternative approach is to use MAGMA to identify drugs that are enriched for connections to genes associated with the GWAS phenotype. We use the collection of bipartite gene-drug interactions collated by DrugTargetor. Unlike the TWAS-CMAP approaches, the MAGMA based approach does not consider the direction of effect of the gene on the GWAS phenotype or the drug on the genes expression/function, so may highlight drugs that might increase risk of the GWAS phenotype. However, the MAGMA approach can use a broader and perhaps more reliable sources of drug-gene interaction databases. To help validate the approaches used for identifying drug repurposing oppurtunities, we test for enrichment of drugs within ATC classifications.
